recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

(13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

Install and maintain approved smoke detectors. (13-196-100 thru 13-196-160) Install a smoke detector in every dwelling unit. Install one on any living level with a habitable room or unenclosed heating plant, on the uppermost ceiling of enclosed porch stairwell, and within 15 feet of every sleeping room. Be sure the detector is at least 4 inches from the wall, 4 to 12 inches from the ceiling, and not above door or window.

Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

MANAGEMENT IS ACTIVELY OFFERING CASH FOR KEYS SO AS TO ENCOURAGE THE NUMEROUS NON-RENT PAYING TENANTS TO LEAVE IN LIEU OF EVICTION. AS THIS PROGRAM PROCEEDS, APARTMENTS ARE BECOMING VACANT. recent_violations.ordinance: Repair or replace
recent_violations.inspector_comments: THIS 3 STORY BUILDING HAS NUMEROUS EXTERIOR DOORS IN A STATE OF SEVERE DISREPAIR. THIS NARRATIVE WILL REFER TO EACH AND EVERY EXTERIOR FRONT ENTRY DOOR AT GRADE; EACH AND EVERY BALCONY ACCESS DOOR AND ANY OF THE APARTMENT FRONT DOORS IN DISREPAIR (SOME OF THE  APARTMENT ENTRANCE DOORS ARE OPERABLE). ALL OF THE AFFECTED DOORS SHARE THE FOLLOWING DEFECTS; DAMAGED OR MISSING LOCK HARDWARE, DAMAGED OR MISSING SELF-CLOSING DEVICES, DAMAGED HINGES, DAMAGED DOOR FRAMES, DOORS NOT CLOSING FLUSH WITH DOOR FRAME AND DOORS NOT LOCKING. THE POOR CONDITION OF THE FRONT EXTERIOR BUILDING ENTRANCE DOORS, AS WELL AS BALCONY ACCESS DOORS, HAS RENDERED THIS ENTIRE BUILDING AS UNSECURE. THERE IS ABSOLUTELY NO BASIC BUILDING SECURITY AS A RESULT OF THE EXTERIOR DOORS(S) CONDITION. ALSO, MOST OF THE STORM / SCREEN DOORS ARE MISSING / INOPERABLE. THIS CONDITION IS TO BE CONSIDERED DANGEROUS AND HAZARDOUS. ALL AFFECTED DOORS ARE TO BE REPLACED WITH NEW DOOR & FRAME SETS. PERMIT REQUIRED.SECTION 14X-3-303.13, 14X-3-303.17 AND 14X-12-1202.4.3.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Repair or replace
recent_violations.inspector_comments: THIS 3 STORY BUILDING HAS NUMEROUS EXTERIOR DOORS IN A STATE OF SEVERE DISREPAIR. THIS NARRATIVE WILL REFER TO EACH AND EVERY EXTERIOR FRONT ENTRY DOOR AT GRADE; EACH AND EVERY BALCONY ACCESS DOOR AND ANY OF THE APARTMENT FRONT DOORS IN DISREPAIR (SOME OF THE  APARTMENT ENTRANCE DOORS ARE OPERABLE). ALL OF THE AFFECTED DOORS SHARE THE FOLLOWING DEFECTS; DAMAGED OR MISSING LOCK HARDWARE, DAMAGED OR MISSING SELF-CLOSING DEVICES, DAMAGED HINGES, DAMAGED DOOR FRAMES, DOORS NOT CLOSING FLUSH WITH DOOR FRAME AND DOORS NOT LOCKING. THE POOR CONDITION OF THE FRONT EXTERIOR BUILDING ENTRANCE DOORS, AS WELL AS BALCONY ACCESS DOORS, HAS RENDERED THIS ENTIRE BUILDING AS UNSECURE. THERE IS ABSOLUTELY NO BASIC BUILDING SECURITY AS A RESULT OF THE EXTERIOR DOORS(S) CONDITION. ALSO, MOST OF THE STORM / SCREEN DOORS ARE MISSING / INOPERABLE. THIS CONDITION IS TO BE CONSIDERED DANGEROUS AND HAZARDOUS. ALL AFFECTED DOORS ARE TO BE REPLACED WITH NEW DOOR & FRAME SETS. PERMIT REQUIRED.SECTION 14X-3-303.13, 14X-3-303.17 AND 14X-12-1202.4.3.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.inspector_comments: AS PER SECTION 17-2-0207-B (11),A TRANSITIONAL RESIDENCE IN A PARCEL CLASSIFIED RS-3 RERQUIRES A SPECIAL USE PERMIT. AT THE TIME OF INSPECTION, THE FOLLOWING FLOOR OCCUPANCY WAS OBSERVED; 1ST FLOOR HAS 2 BEDROOMS, ONE IS OCCUPIED BY 2 MALES AND THE SECOND IS USED AS AN OFFICE. THE ATTIC HAS 2 BEDROOMS, ONE IS OCCUPIED BY 3 MALES AND THE SECOND BY 1 MALE. THE BASEMENT AREA HAS 2 BEDROOMS, ONE IS OCCUPIED BY 2 MALES AND THE SECOND BY 1 MALE. THE TOTAL HEAD COUNT IS 9 INDIVIDUALS WITH NON-FAMILIAL TIES RESIDING TOGETHER. A SUBSEQUENT PERMIT SEARCH DIDN'T IDENTIFY A SPECIAL USE PERMIT ON FILE.

recent_violations.ordinance: Provide
recent_violations.inspector_comments: AS PER SECTION 14A-4-401.1, IT'S UNLAWFUL TO CONSTRUCT, ALTER, REHABILITATE OR CHANGE THE OCCUPANCY WITHOUT FIRST OBTAINING A PERMIT. AT THE TIME OF INSPECTION, THE FOLLOWING-BUT NOT LIMITED TO, INTERIOR AND EXTERIOR ALTERATIONS WERE OBSERVED; THE ORIGINAL PORCH SYSTEM AT THE REAR WAS ENCLOSED AND ATTACHED TO THE REAR OF THE HOUSE. A NEW EXTERIOR STAIR SYSTEM WITH A HANDICAP RAMP WAS CONSTRUCTED AT THE REAR, 6FT SOLID WOOD FENCING WAS ERECTED AT THE REAR OF THE LOT ENCLOSING THE YARD AREA AND SEPARATING THE PARKING AREA. THE FIRST FLOOR HAD THE INTERIOR OF THE KITCHEN AREA ENLARGED BY REMOVING THE ORIGINAL EXTERIOR WALL AND ANNEXING THE ENCLOSED PORCH SYSTEM AS ADDITIONAL LIVING SPACE. THE STAIR SYSTEM TO THE ATTIC WAS MODIFIED TO ACCESS THE ATTIC SPACE AREA, WHEREAT 2 BEDROOMS AND A HALF BATHROOM WERE FORMED. THE BASEMENT AREA WAS TRANFORMED FROM INCIDENTAL STORAGE AND MECHANICAL AREA TO INCLUDE 2 BEDROOMS, A FULL BATHROOM, LAUNDRY AREA, LOUNGE AREA, FURNACE AND WATER HEATER MECHANICAL ROOM. A SUBSEQUENT PERMIT SEARCH DIDN'T IDENTIFY THE REQUIRED PERMIT FOR ALL LISTED ALTERATIONS THAT INCLUDES, ELECTRICAL, PLUMBING AND HVAC ALTERATIONS/ADDITIONS. DUE TO THE EXTENSIVE ALTERATIONS INSIDE AND OUT, A DETAILED ARCHITECTURAL PLAN AND RENOVATION PERMIT IS NOW REQUIRED TO LEGALIZE ALL WORK PERFORMED WITHOUT A PERMIT.

PROVIDE ROUGH INSPECTION FOR INSTALLATION OF ELECTRICAL CONDUIT,BOXES,WIRING,DEVICES AND ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT INSTALLED THRU OUT THE BASEMENT,1,2 FLOOR AREAS WITHOUT ROUGH INSPECTION; ROUGH INSPECTION REQUIRES THAT ALL WALLS AND CEILING BE OPEN TO CONDUCT A COMPLETE ROUGH INSPECTION        14A-5-505.2

The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Repair or replace
recent_violations.inspector_comments: THIS 3 STORY BUILDING HAS NUMEROUS EXTERIOR DOORS IN A STATE OF SEVERE DISREPAIR. THIS NARRATIVE WILL REFER TO EACH AND EVERY EXTERIOR FRONT ENTRY DOOR AT GRADE; EACH AND EVERY BALCONY ACCESS DOOR AND ANY OF THE APARTMENT FRONT DOORS IN DISREPAIR (SOME OF THE  APARTMENT ENTRANCE DOORS ARE OPERABLE). ALL OF THE AFFECTED DOORS SHARE THE FOLLOWING DEFECTS; DAMAGED OR MISSING LOCK HARDWARE, DAMAGED OR MISSING SELF-CLOSING DEVICES, DAMAGED HINGES, DAMAGED DOOR FRAMES, DOORS NOT CLOSING FLUSH WITH DOOR FRAME AND DOORS NOT LOCKING. THE POOR CONDITION OF THE FRONT EXTERIOR BUILDING ENTRANCE DOORS, AS WELL AS BALCONY ACCESS DOORS, HAS RENDERED THIS ENTIRE BUILDING AS UNSECURE. THERE IS ABSOLUTELY NO BASIC BUILDING SECURITY AS A RESULT OF THE EXTERIOR DOORS(S) CONDITION. ALSO, MOST OF THE STORM / SCREEN DOORS ARE MISSING / INOPERABLE. THIS CONDITION IS TO BE CONSIDERED DANGEROUS AND HAZARDOUS. ALL AFFECTED DOORS ARE TO BE REPLACED WITH NEW DOOR & FRAME SETS. PERMIT REQUIRED.SECTION 14X-3-303.13, 14X-3-303.17 AND 14X-12-1202.4.3.

ALSO, BOTH THE TAVERN (3923) AND THE COMMERCIAL SPACE (3925) HAVE BEEN JOINED TO A LARGE 1 STORY SPACE BEHIND THE 2 FRONT SPACES (3923-25) VIA A BREACH IN THE REAR WALLS OF (3923-3925). THE RESULTING CONFIGURATION CONTAINS, IN ADDITION TO THE ORIGINAL TAVERN (3923) AND ORIGINAL COMMERCIAL SPACE (3925), A BILLIARDS ROOM WITH FIXED SEATING (3925) AND A LARGE PPA SPACE IN THE REAR STRUCTURE BEHIND (3923-25). THIS REAR STRUCTURE CONTAINS A PERFORMANCE STAGE, FIXED SEATING, A DANCE FLOOR AND A FIXED DJ BOOTH WITH SOUND SYSTEM. A LIVE BAND SET UP WITH MUSICAL INSTRUMENTS EXISTS ON THE PERFORMANCE STAGE.THERE ARE NO LICENCES FOR THE (3925) ROOM OR THE PPA SPACE AT THE REAR (3923-25 REAR). THE DOB HAS ISSUED A CLOSURE FOR THE ENTIRE PREMISES.SECTION 14A-4-401.1

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

(13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

Install and maintain approved smoke detectors. (13-196-100 thru 13-196-160) Install a smoke detector in every dwelling unit. Install one on any living level with a habitable room or unenclosed heating plant, on the uppermost ceiling of enclosed porch stairwell, and within 15 feet of every sleeping room. Be sure the detector is at least 4 inches from the wall, 4 to 12 inches from the ceiling, and not above door or window.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

(13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

(13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Repair or replace
recent_violations.inspector_comments: THIS 3 STORY BUILDING HAS NUMEROUS EXTERIOR DOORS IN A STATE OF SEVERE DISREPAIR. THIS NARRATIVE WILL REFER TO EACH AND EVERY EXTERIOR FRONT ENTRY DOOR AT GRADE; EACH AND EVERY BALCONY ACCESS DOOR AND ANY OF THE APARTMENT FRONT DOORS IN DISREPAIR (SOME OF THE  APARTMENT ENTRANCE DOORS ARE OPERABLE). ALL OF THE AFFECTED DOORS SHARE THE FOLLOWING DEFECTS; DAMAGED OR MISSING LOCK HARDWARE, DAMAGED OR MISSING SELF-CLOSING DEVICES, DAMAGED HINGES, DAMAGED DOOR FRAMES, DOORS NOT CLOSING FLUSH WITH DOOR FRAME AND DOORS NOT LOCKING. THE POOR CONDITION OF THE FRONT EXTERIOR BUILDING ENTRANCE DOORS, AS WELL AS BALCONY ACCESS DOORS, HAS RENDERED THIS ENTIRE BUILDING AS UNSECURE. THERE IS ABSOLUTELY NO BASIC BUILDING SECURITY AS A RESULT OF THE EXTERIOR DOORS(S) CONDITION. ALSO, MOST OF THE STORM / SCREEN DOORS ARE MISSING / INOPERABLE. THIS CONDITION IS TO BE CONSIDERED DANGEROUS AND HAZARDOUS. ALL AFFECTED DOORS ARE TO BE REPLACED WITH NEW DOOR & FRAME SETS. PERMIT REQUIRED.SECTION 14X-3-303.13, 14X-3-303.17 AND 14X-12-1202.4.3.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.inspector_comments: MOST APARTMENTS HAVE DAMAGED CLOSET DOORS WITH DEFECTS RANGING FROM DAMAGED SLIDE RAILS, DOORS COMPLETELY OFF RAILS, DOORS THAT DO NO CLOSE EASILY OR FLUSH WITH THE FRAME. REPAIR OR REPLACE EACH AND EVERY CLOSET DOOR SET IN EVERY APARTMENT.SECTION 114X=3-304.6.

recent_violations.ordinance: Repair or replace
recent_violations.inspector_comments: THIS 3 STORY BUILDING HAS NUMEROUS EXTERIOR DOORS IN A STATE OF SEVERE DISREPAIR. THIS NARRATIVE WILL REFER TO EACH AND EVERY EXTERIOR FRONT / REAR ENTRY DOOR AT GRADE; EACH AND EVERY BALCONY ACCESS DOOR AND ANY OF THE APARTMENT FRONT DOORS IN DISREPAIR (SOME OF THE APARTMENT ENTRANCE DOORS ARE OPERABLE). ALL OF THE AFFECTED DOORS SHARE THE FOLLOWING DEFECTS; DAMAGED OR MISSING LOCK HARDWARE, DAMAGED OR MISSING SELF-CLOSING DEVICES, DAMAGED HINGES, DAMAGED DOOR FRAMES, DOORS NOT CLOSING FLUSH WITH DOOR FRAME AND DOORS NOT LOCKING. THE POOR CONDITION OF THE FRONT / REAR EXTERIOR BUILDING ENTRANCE DOORS, AS WELL AS BALCONY ACCESS DOORS, HAS RENDERED THIS ENTIRE BUILDING AS UNSECURE. THERE IS ABSOLUTELY NO BASIC BUILDING SECURITY AS A RESULT OF THE EXTERIOR DOORS(S) CONDITION. ALSO, MOST OF THE STORM / SCREEN DOORS ARE MISSING / INOPERABLE. THIS CONDITION IS TO BE CONSIDERED DANGEROUS AND HAZARDOUS. ALL AFFECTED DOORS ARE TO BE REPLACED WITH NEW DOOR & FRAME SETS. PERMIT REQUIRED.SECTION 14X-3-303.13, 14X-3-303.17 AND 14X-12-1202.4.3.

In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.inspector_comments: AS PER SECTION 14A-4-401.1, IT'S UNLAWFUL TO CONSTRUCT, ENLARGE, REHABILITATE, ALTER AND/OR CHANGE THE OCCUPANCY WITHOUT FIRST OBTAINING A PERMIT.AT THE TIME OF INSPECTION, THE OCCUPANCY WAS AS FOLLOWS.1ST FLOOR HAS A SINGLE DWELLING UNIT.2ND FLOOR HAS A SINGLE DWELLING UNIT.3RD FLOOR HAS A SINGLE DWELLING UNIT.A SUBSEQUENT  PERMIT SEARCH FOUND WATER RECORDS THAT INDICATE A DIFFERENT OCCUPANCY.THE FIRST FLOOR HAD A FRONT COMMERCIAL UNIT AND A REAR RESIDENTIAL UNIT.THE SECOND FLOOR HAD FRONT AND REAR DWELLING UNITS.THE THIRD FLOOR HAD FRONT AND REAR DWELLING UNITS.ALL LEVELS WERE REHABILITATED AND MODERNIZED, NEW FLOOR LAYOUT INTRODUCED BY COMBINING FRONT AND REAR UNITS INTO A SINGLE DWELLING UNIT PER FLOOR. OTHER ALTERATIONS, SUCH AS THE BRICK-IN DOOR OPENING AT THE EAST ELEVATION, AND THE ADDITION OF A DECORATIVE CONCRETE BLOCK GARAGE CONSTRUCTED AT THE REAR OF THE LOT, WERE PERFOMED WITHOUT PLANS AND PERMITS.DUE TO THE EXTENSIVE INTERIOR AND EXTERIOR ALTERATIONS, COUPLED WITH OCCUPANCY CHANGES AFFECTING ALL DISCIPLINES, A DETAILED ARCHITECTURAL PLAN IS NOW REQUIRED TO LEGALIZE ALL ALTERATIONS AND/OR CONSTRUCTION.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

REPORT SHALL BE SIGNED AND SEALED BY A REGISTERED DESIGN PROFESSIONAL, AND BASED ON A CRITICAL, COMPREHENSIVE, AND DETAILED PHYSICAL INSPECTION OF THE PREMISES IDENTIFIED AND DETAILED IN THE VIOLATION. THE CONDITION REPORT MUST IDENTIFY THE DATE, NATURE, SCOPE, FINDINGS, AND DEFICIENCIES OF THE INSPECTION/INVESTIGATION. THE REPORT MUST IDENTIFY EACH TECHNICAL PRINCIPLE OR STANDARD THAT IS THE BASIS OF ANY PROFESSIONAL JUDGMENT AND COMPREHENSIVE RECOMMENDATIONS FOR REPAIRS EXPRESSED IN THE REPORT. RECOMMENDATION OF REPAIRS MUST INCLUDE PHOTOS, DRAWINGS, DETAILS, AND CALCULATIONS WHICH CAN BE SUBMITTED FOR A REPAIR PERMIT IF NECESSARY. THE CONDITION REPORT, PERMIT, AND CONSTRUCTION DOCUMENTS MUST BE KEPT ON FILE AT THE PREMISES AND MADE AVAILABLE FOR FIELD INSPECTION REVIEW AND APPROVAL BY ALL RELATED TRADES. SUBMIT ELECTRONIC REPORT FOR REVIEW AND APPROVAL TO: DOB_CAR@CITYOFCHICAGO.ORG (14X-1-104.1 THRU 14X-1-104.4, 14A-6-603.5, AND 14A-4-411.1) [SPECIFY ELEMENT AND LOCATION].

Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.
recent_violations.inspector_comments: MISSING CARBON MONOXIDE DETECTOR.

Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.inspector_comments: THE 1ST FLOOR COMMERCIAL SPACE IS OPERATING AS AN ONGOING PPA EVENT SPACE WITHOUT PLANS / PERMITS / LICENSES. ON THE NIGHT OF THIS INSPECTION THIS TASK FORCE (DOB, BACP, CPD) STOPPED A PARTY IN ITS' EARLY STAGES. 50 OF THE 250 GUEST (INVITED / PAID TICKET HIOLDERS) HAD ARRIVED. THE LIVE BAND WAS SETTING UP AND THE BAR WAS BEING STOCKED. THIS COMMERCIAL STOREFRONT HAS BEEN ALTERED INTO A NOW EXISTING NIGHT CLUB / EVENT SPACE. THIS 1ST FLOOR ALTERATION EXTENDS FROM THE BUILDING FRONT ALL THE WAY BACK TO THE ALLEY (150'). THE FRONT PORTION OF THIS BUILDING IS 2 STORIES WITH AN ATTIC. ALL OF THE 1ST FLOOR LOAD BEARING WALLS HAVE BEEN REMOVED WITHOUT PLANS / PERMITS. EXTENSIVE ELECTRICAL / PLUMBING / HAVC WORK HAS BEEN PERFORMED, BY UNLICENSED PERSONNELL, WITHOUT PLANS / PERMITS. THE PROPRIETOR OF THIS EVENT CALLED DOB TO DENY ANY EVENT OCCURRED. THIS INSPECTOR, WITH 4 BACP INVESTIGATORS AN 12 CPD OFFICERS,  WOULD STIPULATE OTHERWISE.THE ONLY AVENUE TO LEGALIZE THIS 1ST FLOOR EVENT SPACE WOULD BE ACQUIRING A PPA LICENSE. ARCHITECTURAL DRAWINGS SUBMITTED WITH ZONING APPROVAL WOULD BE NEEDE ABSOLUTELY IN ORDER TO PROCEED. SHORT OF THAT EFFORT, THIS SPACE IS TO REMAIN COMPLETELY CLOSED TO ALL ACTIVITIES. ALSO, IF NO PPA LICENSE ACQUISITION IS ATTEMPTED, ARCHITECTURAL DRAWING ARE STILL REUIRED FOR THE EXTENSIVE WORK ALREADY PERFORMED WITHOUT SAID PLANS AND PERMITS.THE EVENT WAS SHUT DOWN BY THIS TASK FORCE AND THE 1ST FLOOR SPACE WAS VACATED AND LOCKED.BACP / DOB CLOSURES WERE ISSUED.SECTION 14A-4-401.1

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

(13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

(13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.
